..
Issued at 226 PM EDT Mon Aug 24 2026

Early afternoon GOES-East imagery shows mostly clear skies over the 
UP except for a few fair weather cu along the western UP highlands 
and sine low clouds along the shores of eastern Lake Superior where 
moisture and forcing is still marginally present associated with a 
RAP-analyzed 1007mb low over the Ontario/Quebec line. A 1018 mb 
surface high extends from western Lake Superior to Illinois which is 
providing the clear skies elsewhere and allowing temperatures to 
climb back into the mid 60s after an autumn-feeling morning. With 
efficient radiational warming expected today, expect highs to 
reach into the 70s except immediately along the Lake Superior 
shoreline along the east half, where continued brisk 
northwesterlies are leading to Lake Superior-cooled air to be 
advected onshore. These winds are also driving wave heights of 
3-6 feet from 1-5 miles from shore along Alger and Luce County 
shorelines today, which will drive a high risk of dangerous rip 
currents. Therefore, the Beach Hazards Statement will continue 
through this evening, though the swim risk drops significantly 
tonight as the high pressure fully establishes itself over the 
UP and wind speeds similarly decrease. Another mostly clear 
night tonight will allow temperatures to fall to their dew 
points for many interior locations, with the HREF giving pockets
of 20-40% chances of fog formation especially in the east. 
Temperatures should be too high for frost, though a few interior
locations may fall into the upper 30s.

By 12Z Tuesday, the upper air pattern consists of a massive ridge 
over the south-central to southwestern CONUS flanked by a pair of 
deep troughs, one over Quebec and off the Pacific Northwest coast 
respectively. Additionally, a trough will be over southern Manitoba 
and will pivot around the ridge into the Great Lakes region for the 
midweek period, bringing a period of active weather. With the CAMs 
now beginning to cover this time period, the consensus on the 
arrival time of showers in the west with the prefrontal isentropic 
ascent has accelerated, with the HREF mean arrival time of precip 
now showing shortly after noon Tuesday at IWD and around 22Z for the 
US41/141 corridor. Moist southerly flow ahead of the cold front will 
allow for dew points to climb into the low 60s and for PWATs to grow 
to 1.25-1.5 inches in the west, which is above the 85th percentile 
of climatology for this time of year. This will promote an unstable 
airmass with HREF mean SBCAPE values in the west ballooning to 
around 750 J/kg by 23Z Tuesday. However, shear is relatively 
unimpressive as soundings show flow is sub-30 kt below 525mb, though 
the low level hodographs do show good curvature. Therefore, will 
expect mostly sub-severe thunderstorms as buoyancy is sufficient 
with weak forcing and not enough shear to keep storms organized 
enough. 

Overnight into early Wednesday, showers and thunderstorms overspread 
the UP. If storms can maintain elevated from the boundary layer, the 
Euro ensemble projects they will have 500-750 J/kg of MUCAPE to work 
with, though shear remains subpar with weak flow aloft, so overnight 
thunderstorms are not expected to be severe. Diurnal destabilization 
will reinvigorate storms during the afternoon Wednesday as Euro mean 
MUCAPE will climb to near 1000 J/kg for much of the east half. Even 
if storms remain sub-severe for most, a good soaking rain is 
expected as LREF probabilities of over a half inch of rain are 40-
60% for most.

Lingering northerly flow behind the shortwave will allow 
temperatures aloft to fall to similar temperatures that caused light 
lake effect rain showers yesterday, so some PoPs will linger into 
Thursday. Over the last 24 hours, confidence has increased in high 
pressure settling over the Great Lakes Friday into the weekend, 
leading to dry weather. While the models differ in the details, the 
global deterministic suite has come into increasing agreement that 
the ridge aloft will shift to the southeast CONUS and bring with it 
a more potent trough through the Great Lakes in the early portions 
of next week, which could bring unsettled weather to the UP as soon 
as late Saturday and Sunday.
